subject: Clarify token quantum, context-length rounding, and mini-pilot billing
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@lighthouselabs.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lighthouse Labs Procurement <procurement@lighthouselabs.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarification on billing quantum and small-pilot math

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Lighthouse Labs is excited about the latency profile and the Dedicated trial. Before we sign the pilot, procurement asked for one last clarification on how you bill micro-usage for our PoC: specifically, how tokens are rounded, how long-context sessions are bucketed, and whether there are any minimums that would surprise a weekly/low-traffic workload.

Attached is a sample of our expected weekly usage (CSV) and a small sketch of a 5k-context embedding+chat pattern. Key questions:
- If a single API call returns 1,250 tokens, do you round up to a 1,000-token slab, 1,250, or to the next quantum?
- How do you treat very long-context cases where payloads exceed 16k tokens but are broken into prefix + streaming segments — are those merged for billing or billed per-request?
- For pilots under 50k tokens/month, do you apply any minimums or commit floors that would effectively make the pilot cost higher than expected?

Procurement would like the answers in writing to attach to the SOW. Appreciate a crisp explanation we can share.

Best,
Alice
Alice Tan
Director of ML Engineering
Lighthouse Labs

P.S. If it helps, we can hop on a quick call with your billing team later this week.
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@lighthouselabs.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on billing quantum and small-pilot math

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the note and the usage sample — super helpful. Short answers up front, then I9ll give the exact rules so your procurement team has copy-paste language for the SOW: 

1) Rounding/quantum for per-call token charges: we meter at the token level and bill in 250-token quanta for generation calls (so 1,250 tokens rounds to 1,250 exactly; charges are computed in 250-token increments internally, but we report exact tokens on invoices).

2) Long-context requests: we attempt to collapse prefix + streamed segments into a single session for metering when they share a consistent session id and occur within the same hour; otherwise they are billed per-request.

3) Pilot minimums: for pilot customers under 100k tokens/month we do not apply an invoice minimum by default; however, Dedicated capacity pilots sometimes have a modest reserved seat minimum tied to GPU uptime (we9d disclose any such minimum in the SOW). For Lighthouse9s standard hosted pilot there would be no surprise floor.

I9m cc9ing Marissa and Jonas from pricing to confirm and add any nuance on the Dedicated pilot side. I9ll also put a short doc excerpt below you can paste into procurement.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

-----Forwarded excerpt (billing language you can paste):
Redwood invoices reflect exact token usage; generation token quantities are rounded to internal 250-token quanta for calculation but invoices list exact tokens and prorated charges. Long-context requests that are linked by session id and processed within the same hour will be merged for metering to avoid double-counting. Dedicated capacity pilots may include a disclosed reserved uptime minimum; hosted pilot arrangements under 100k tokens/month have no automatic invoice minimums.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Quick clarification on billing quantum and small-pilot math

Camila / team,

A couple of technical clarifications for the SOW blurb and an ask for the procurement note:

1) Quantum specifics: we bill generation tokens in 250-token calculation quanta as Camila said, but we also have a separate embedding-metering quantum of 10 vectors per call for embedding endpoints (important if they batch embeddings). We should call that out because their CSV shows mixed embed+chat patterns.

2) Long-context merge window nuance: the "same hour" rule is our default heuristic but we actually use a sliding 60-minute merge window tied to the session9s last activity. If a request arrives 59 minutes after a prior request with same session id we merge; at 61 minutes we do not. We also have an opt-in config for customers to widen that window to 24 hours for more aggressive session aggregation (useful for low-traffic mobile apps). This opt-in is a per-account flag and requires ops approval.

3) Pilot committed-bare-metal caveat: their PoC looks like Dedicated is on the table. For Dedicated pilots that reserve GPU shards, we typically require a small uptime credit (10% of a GPU instance-hour minimum) which we reconcile against usage. For hosted pilots we don9t apply that.

4) Suggested procurement language: I9ve drafted a short paragraph to paste into SOWs (see below). Can we add the embed quantum sentence before we send?

Regards,
Marissa
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference

Suggested SOW paragraph (draft):
Redwood9s billing reflects measured token and embedding usage. Generation requests are calculated in 250-token quanta and billed at actual tokens reported on invoices. Embedding calls are charged per-vector with a 10-vector per-call measurement quantum for batching. Session-affiliated requests that share a session identifier and occur within a 60-minute sliding window are aggregated for metering to avoid double-counting. Dedicated capacity pilots that reserve GPU shards may include a disclosed reserved uptime minimum; hosted pilots under 100k tokens/month do not carry an invoice minimum.

Hi Alice — following up with the agreed wording for procurement and a couple of attachments for transparency.

TL;DR (copy/paste for SOW):
Redwood charges generation token usage with internal 250-token calculation quanta; invoices list exact tokens and prorated charges. Embedding requests are metered per-vector with a 10-vector per-call measurement quantum to support efficient batching. Requests tied by session id and processed within a 60-minute sliding activity window are merged for metering; customers can request an extended aggregation window (up to 24 hours) for low-traffic workloads via an account flag (requires ops approval). Dedicated capacity pilots that reserve GPU shards include a disclosed reserved-uptime minimum; hosted pilots below 100k tokens/month do not have an invoice minimum.
